warnings: There is NO grade-A evidence in this run. No lawfully collected AI conversations, interviews, on-site search logs, support tickets or paid-search exports were supplied. The best available evidence is grade B: public forum comments with permalinks, dated independent reporting, and search-result-shape proxies.
Language samples below are short public spans or faithful paraphrases. Counts inside a source are counts within that source and are never relabelled as market frequency.
No job below asserts prevalence. 'Recurring' means recurring across the retrieved sources, not across the market.
job-011 is a measurement construct for control cells, not a demand finding.

jobs.statement: When automated clients consume a site's content at a scale that raises hosting cost without returning readers, help the site operator regain control over which automated clients may access the content while keeping human and search discoverability intact.
jobs.struggling_moment: Server load and bandwidth cost rise while human readership stays flat; the operator cannot tell how much of the traffic is automated or which parts to allow.
jobs.desired_progress: A defensible, selective access policy: search crawlers allowed, training/agent crawlers governed, humans unaffected.

Server-level blocking, rate limiting and IP/UA bans when directives are ignored
Blocking entire countries in extreme cases

pull.text: Emerging option to be paid rather than merely scraped

anxiety.text: Losing search traffic by blocking too broadly

habit.text: robots.txt is the familiar lever even though a rising share of requests ignore it

criteria.text: Distinguishes search indexing from training/agent use

constraints.text: Ad-bearing pages are treated differently under the 2026-09-15 default change

jobs.statement: When a business-critical website is unreachable under a flood of requests, help an operator without security staff restore availability now and stop it recurring.
jobs.struggling_moment: Site is down or timing out; the host attributes it to request volume; the operator does not know whether it is an attack or organic and has no playbook.
jobs.desired_progress: Site back up within the hour, with a durable setting or service that prevents the next occurrence.

workarounds.text: Call the host and ask them to mitigate
Turn on stricter protection settings reactively

push.text: Downtime during peak hours is a direct revenue and trust loss

pull.text: Packaged protection bundled with delivery is presented as the low-effort fix

anxiety.text: Fear of breaking the site further while under load

habit.text: Defaults to the hosting provider as first responder

constraints.text: Budget in the low tens-to-hundreds per month band

jobs.struggling_moment: Recurring overage or egress charges with no clear picture of which requests drive them.
jobs.desired_progress: A measurable reduction in origin traffic and transfer cost with no functional regression.

Bandwidth-alliance style peering arrangements and cheaper origin storage
Splitting media onto a second provider or a higher tier

anxiety.text: Caching aggressively may break dynamic behaviour

jobs.struggling_moment: Vendor marketing does not answer the questions that actually decide the contract: how it behaves under failure, how it bills, what it is certified for, and whether the team can operate it.
jobs.desired_progress: A defensible shortlist with the differences stated in operational terms.

anxiety.text: Compliance blockers such as cloud-specific certifications and data residency

jobs.statement: When a single upstream provider's failure takes an entire stack offline, help the architecture owner find and reduce that dependency without duplicating every system.
jobs.struggling_moment: An outage in one external provider cascaded through services that were assumed independent; nobody has a map of where else that assumption holds.
jobs.desired_progress: A dependency map and a proportionate fallback for the highest-impact paths.

workarounds.text: Second-vendor quotes and partial multi-provider setups

push.text: A four-hour network-wide provider outage on 2025-11-18 with cascading internal dependencies

anxiety.text: Running two of everything is unaffordable

habit.text: Architectures implicitly assume the provider is always there

language_samples.text: if an architecture assumes the provider is always there, the provider is by definition a single point of failure

jobs.statement: When remote staff, contractors and automated build systems still reach internal applications through a legacy VPN, help the IT or security engineer provide per-request verified access without requiring a persistent client on every machine.
jobs.struggling_moment: The VPN is slow, grants network-wide access after a single node compromise, and cannot be installed on ephemeral CI compute.
jobs.desired_progress: Identity- and posture-verified access per request, covering human and non-human clients.

workarounds.text: Mesh VPN overlays, which still grant tailnet-wide access on node compromise
Self-hosted access proxies that consume engineering time

push.text: Over-permissive network-level access and CI clients that cannot run an agent

pull.text: Continuous verification instead of login-time-only checks

anxiety.text: Migration risk and per-user pricing at scale

habit.text: VPN remains the default because it already exists

criteria.text: Agentless paths for unmanaged and ephemeral clients

constraints.text: Cannot install a client on ephemeral CI runners

language_samples.text: VPN model grants network-wide access if a node is compromised; true zero-trust requires per-request evaluation
configuring access clients on ephemeral compute (CI/CD) is impractical

jobs.struggling_moment: Vendor answers claim full coverage; the team cannot tell which services are native, which are OEM'd, and which apply only to a narrow traffic subset.
jobs.desired_progress: A scoring matrix that survives procurement review.
